summary: Browser redirect delivery vehicle to hardcoded rotating domain
details: px8my ships px.js (declared as the package `main`) whose sole functional behavior is to inject a full-viewport fixed-position iframe (z-index 2147483647) pointing at the hardcoded URL https://mfmz.85qbv.cn/H.html?c=0gjr, overlay a Chinese loading mask, and rewrite the page title. Any site that includes this package (typically via the npm→jsDelivr CDN path npm/px8my/px.js) hands every visitor to the author-controlled endpoint. The tarball also ships update_px8my.sh, a maintainer script that rewrites the mfmz.* redirect domain in px.js, bumps the version, runs `npm publish`, and issues a purge against purge.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js — indicating the package is operated as a rotating redirect vehicle designed to evade domain blocklists via CDN cache invalidation. The package advertises no legitimate utility; its only code path is the covert redirect. This is silent-relay of consumer traffic to a hardcoded author-controlled destination, disguised as a normal library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
